facts.claim: Voyager 1 is the farthest human-made object from Earth, currently in interstellar space.
Voyager 1 was launched by NASA on September 5, 1977, from Cape Canaveral, Florida.
Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause and entered interstellar space on August 25, 2012.
Voyager 1 travels at approximately 17 kilometers per second relative to the Sun.
As of 2025, Voyager 1's signal takes about 23 hours to reach Earth (one-way).
Voyager 1 carries the Golden Record, a phonograph record with sounds and images of Earth, curated by Carl Sagan's committee.
Voyager 1 discovered active volcanoes on Jupiter's moon Io in 1979.
Voyager 1 made its closest approach to Saturn on November 12, 1980, flying within 124,000 kilometers of the planet.
Voyager 1's power source is a radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG) that produces about 200 watts at launch, decaying to about 170 watts by 2025.
Voyager 1 carries a camera that took the famous 'Pale Blue Dot' image of Earth from 6 billion kilometers away on February 14, 1990.
The Voyager spacecraft were built by a team led by project scientist Edward Stone, who served for over 50 years.
Voyager 1's thrusters were partially disabled for attitude control, but in 2017 engineers successfully fired backup thrusters that had been dormant for 37 years.
Voyager 1 is expected to run out of power for its instruments around 2025, but may continue to transmit limited data until about 2036.
Voyager 1 is the first spacecraft to have its plasma instrument detect a lack of solar wind, confirming it left the heliosphere.
As of 2025, Voyager 1 is in a region of interstellar space with a density of about 0.055 atoms per cubic centimeter.

hook_ideas: Start with 'This object is 24 billion kilometers away, and you can hear its heartbeat.'
Show a slowly receding mother board and say 'It still talks to Earth, but its message takes a day to arrive.'
Open with the 'Pale Blue Dot' image and the fact that the same camera is now silent, but the probe still calls home.
misconceptions: Voyager 1 has 'left the solar system' – it has crossed the heliopause into interstellar space, but it is still within the Sun's gravitational influence (Oort cloud), so it has not fully left the solar system.

Voyager 1 is the fastest spacecraft ever launched – it is fast but not the fastest; other probes like Parker Solar Probe achieve higher speeds relative to the Sun, though Voyager 1 is still the farthest.
